what_it_measured.text: The study was designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a test product Semaglutide injection compared with the reference biologic in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
The incidence of ADA and nAb at week 24 was also assessed as a secondary endpoint.

dose.text: All patients received an initial dose of 0.25 mg once weekly for 4 weeks, followed by up-titration to 0.5 mg once weekly at week 4. At week 8, patients with HbA1c <7.5% continued 0.5 mg, whereas those with HbA1c ≥ 7.5% were up-titrated to 1 mg once weekly. Further dose adjustments were performed at weeks 12, 16, and 20 using a treat-totarget approach: patients with HbA1c <7.5% continued their ongoing dose; patients with HbA1c ≥ 7.5% on 0.5 mg were up-titrated to 1 mg, and those on 1 mg were up-titrated to 2 mg once weekly. Patients with HbA1c ≥ 7.5% receiving 2 mg continued the same dose and received rescue medication as per predefined rescue criteria.

route.text: Both the test and comparator products were administered once weekly at any time of day, with or without meals, for 24 weeks as a subcutaneous injection in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm.

endpoint.text: The primary endpoint was analysed using a repeated measures ANCOVA model with baseline HbA1c as covariate and treatment group as a fixed effect.
The incidence of ADA and nAb at week 24 was also assessed as a secondary endpoint.
Study outcomes The primary efficacy endpoint was the change in HbA1c from baseline to week 24.
